approach: See abstract for details

problem: Existing stereo image compression methods either sacrifice perceptual quality at low bitrates or fail to maintain consistency across viewpoints.
approach: SDiD uses shared pre-trained diffusion priors with a diffusion prior alignment module and prior transformation structure for distributed stereo compression.
contribution: SDiD requires only one-third the bitrate of state-of-the-art methods (0.02 bpp vs 0.06 bpp) while maintaining depth information.

problem: Benchmark metrics often produce invalid uncertainty estimates or make unrecognized assumptions about generalized accuracy.
approach: Analysis via generalized linear mixed models produces correct estimates of generalized accuracy while efficiently quantifying uncertainty.
contribution: Shows how statistical modeling can improve uncertainty quantification and provides variance decomposition and item difficulty estimates across 22 frontier LLMs.

problem: Manifold-constrained hyper-connections face training instability, prohibitive parameter complexity, and factorial explosion in parametrization.
approach: KromHC uses Kronecker products of smaller doubly stochastic matrices to parametrize residual connections while enforcing manifold constraints.
contribution: Achieves O(n²C) parameter complexity instead of O(n³C) or O(nC·n!) while matching or outperforming SOTA variants.

problem: Molecular property prediction is limited by expensive labeled data, while standard semi-supervised methods rely on label-preserving augmentations that are challenging in the molecular domain.
approach: Semi-supervised training uses ensemble consensus objectives to improve predictive accuracy across molecular datasets and GNN architectures.
contribution: Ensemble consensus training increases robustness and outperforms full supervised ensembles in most cases while reducing calibration error.

problem: Assessing and improving calibration in sequential vision-language-action tasks remains unexplored, especially for partial trajectories.
approach: Formulates sequential calibration for episodic tasks using temporal-difference value estimation as a principled calibration mechanism.
contribution: TD calibration improves performance on simulated and real-robot data by connecting uncertainty calibration to reinforcement learning.

problem: LLMs sometimes overthink and generate unnecessary reasoning steps under uncertainty or with ill-posed queries.
approach: Proposes nonparametric and parametric early stopping methods that monitor uncertainty signals during generation.
contribution: Uncertainty-aware early stopping improves both efficiency and reliability, with especially significant gains for math reasoning.

problem: Current preference prediction relies on analyzing LLM outputs without considering underlying mechanisms.
approach: Mechanistic forecasting probes internal model representations to extract demographic and ideological information from party-encoding components.
contribution: Probing internal knowledge via mechanistic forecasting improves prediction accuracy on election forecasting across 6 national elections.

problem: Significant gap exists between theoretical universal expressivity and practical performance in Graph Neural Networks.
approach: ENGNNs utilize random noise features with enforced equivariance to nodewise noise transformations for enhanced expressivity.
contribution: Reaches theoretical universal expressivity while maintaining linear scalability and achieving performance comparable to expensive high-expressivity models.

problem: Multi-objective combinatorial optimization sacrifices generality, scalability, or theoretical guarantees with existing methods.
approach: Reformulates it as online learning over decomposed decision space, solving position-wise bandit subproblems via adaptive expert-guided construction.
contribution: Achieves 80-98% of specialized solvers performance with two to three orders of magnitude improvement in sample and computational efficiency.

problem: Existing dense video captioning lacks fine-grained, structured temporal narratives with explicit timestamps.
approach: Proposes Omni Dense Captioning with a six-dimensional structural schema for script-like captions, trained via SFT and GRPO with task-specific rewards.
contribution: Surpasses Gemini-2.5-Pro and significantly boosts downstream audio-visual reasoning and temporal grounding capabilities.

problem: Current geometric models of language focus on embedding spaces rather than intrinsic text properties.
approach: Introduces Texture, a text-native word-level discrete curvature signal measuring differential reconciliation between prefix and suffix.
contribution: Establishes text-native curvature paradigm enabling geometry without geometric training for improved long-context inference.

problem: Reconstructing atomistic crystal structures from single noisy STEM projections is an ill-posed inverse problem lacking verification.
approach: AutoMat uses inference-time hypothesis search with closed-loop verification, composing perception, physics modules, and rollback-retry on failure.
contribution: Outperforms SOTA models on STEM2Mat-Bench with 450+ annotated samples across lattice RMSD, formation energy MAE, and structure matching.

problem: Pre-trained vision-language models like CLIP are highly vulnerable to adversarial perturbations that disrupt image-text alignment.
approach: Proposes Self-Calibrated Consistency (SCC) with semantic and spatial consistency modules using soft pseudo-labels and multi-view predictions.
contribution: Consistently improves CLIP zero-shot robustness across 22 benchmarks while maintaining accuracy as a plug-and-play inference strategy.

problem: Classical feature importance metrics are unsuited to graph-structured data with complex dependencies.
approach: Proposes data-, model-, and task-agnostic feature selection based on changes in validation performance upon permuting feature values.
contribution: Rivals tailored feature selection approaches while returning meaningful importance scores before GNN training completes.

problem: Custom diffusion models assume static personalized concepts and are prone to catastrophic forgetting as new concepts are introduced.
approach: Formulates continual personalization as constrained submodular optimization selecting minimal sufficient concept-specific neurons.
contribution: Achieves fusion-free continual personalization by modifying only 0.41% of total parameters per concept while preventing catastrophic forgetting.

problem: Existing EEG generation methods use discrete denoising objectives that inadequately reflect continuous temporal dynamics and spectral structure.
approach: Introduces Just EEG Transformer (JET), a generative framework using conditional flow matching to model EEG as evolving continuous trajectories.
contribution: Reduces TS-FID by over 40% compared to baselines while capturing key EEG structural properties for scalable generation.

problem: PDE neural operators either focus on specific properties or suffer from high computational costs and poor generalization.
approach: Flower uses multihead warps that predict displacement fields and resample adaptively at sparse coordinates for adaptive global interactions.
contribution: Compact 17M-parameter model outperforms Fourier, convolution, and attention baselines on 2D/3D time-dependent PDE benchmarks.

problem: Unclear whether time series participate in multimodal representation convergence observed in vision and language.
approach: Examines trimodal alignment through post-hoc projection heads using contrastive learning with analysis of geometry and scaling behavior.
contribution: Finds asymmetric alignment with time series aligning more strongly to vision, demonstrating images as effective intermediaries.

problem: CodeGen AI security research focuses on red teaming but lacks effective blue teaming defenses requiring deep security analysis.
approach: BlueCodeAgent uses automated red teaming to generate diverse risky instances guiding multi-level blue team defense with constitution summarization.
contribution: Achieves average F1 improvement of 14.7% across four code security tasks with dynamic analysis reducing false positives.

problem: Models degrade under imbalanced samples, inaccurate labels, and backdoor attacks but lack scenario-agnostic optimization methods.
approach: Attributes performance degradation to parameter contamination and recovers clean parameters via implicit manifold autoencoders with diffusion.
contribution: Parameter purification generalizes across imbalanced learning, label noise, and backdoor defense without scenario-specific design.

problem: Distributed training is bottlenecked by optimizer state memory and communication requirements even with low-rank optimizers.
approach: Combines low-rank optimization with infrequent synchronization using full-rank quasi-hyperbolic updates for subspace exploration.
contribution: Achieves near-parity with DDP while reducing communication by ~10x at 125M-720M model scales.

problem: LLMs' token-level generation encourages local decisions and lacks global planning, leading to redundant or inaccurate reasoning.
approach: Two-stage framework where LLMs summarize CoT reasoning into high-level guidance, then joint optimization via guidance-aware RL.
contribution: Delivers stable and significant improvements across mathematics and natural sciences reasoning with five diverse base models.

problem: Steering diffusion models toward unseen conditions requires retraining or per-step gradient computations with substantial overhead.
approach: Combines offline-computed noise alignment and RFM activation steering enabling fast controllable generation without gradient guidance.
contribution: Improves target accuracy over gradient-based guidance with substantial inference speedups across CIFAR-10, ImageNet, CelebA.

problem: Existing agent benchmarks evaluate code-centric or data-centric capabilities in isolation, missing real-world data-intensive scenarios.
approach: Introduces data-intensive Linux sandbox based on Kaggle with 1,009 tasks spanning 31 communities, average 980 files per task.
contribution: Top-performing agents achieve only 61.1% success, highlighting substantial gap in data discovery and code execution integration.

problem: Strategic classification assumes public classifiers but unclear why systems would commit to full disclosure under regulation.
approach: Studies settings where regulation requires partial disclosure, enabling learner to reveal sets of possible classifiers while privately choosing realization.
contribution: Develops efficient algorithms for computing best-responses and training in this ambiguity setting.

problem: Generalized Category Discovery methods rely on semantic labels and global representations, overlooking part-level cues crucial for distinguishing categories.
approach: Incorporates part-level visual feature correspondences to capture finer-grained semantic structures without requiring GCD method modifications.
contribution: Part-level correspondence priors significantly improve existing GCD approaches across multiple benchmarks.

problem: Inference-time guidance for diffusion models requires repeated score/gradient evaluations introducing bias and computational overhead.
approach: URGE performs path-wise importance reweighting via Girsanov change of measure with multiplicative trajectory weights and periodic resampling.
contribution: Outperforms guidance baselines on generation quality while being simpler to implement and fully gradient-free.

problem: SLM-LLM routing methods train routers to mimic LLM trajectories, capping performance at reference limits.
approach: Formulates routing as MDP using Collaborative Inference Tree Search and Tree-Advantage Policy Optimization for credit assignment.
contribution: Advances Pareto frontier of accuracy-efficiency trade-offs by exploiting better inference trajectories in collaborative space.

problem: Slot Attention iterations and recurrences across video frames use inconsistent aggregation transforms due to cold-start query limitations.
approach: Preheats cold-start queries with input-feature information and differentiates aggregation transforms using full and single iterations.
contribution: Improves object discovery, recognition, and visual reasoning through smoothed slot attention across iterations and recurrences.

problem: LLM inference pipelines are stitched together as services obscuring cross-stage interference and limiting pipeline-level optimization.
approach: Treats inference pipelines as first-class compilation targets with declarative dataflows and distributed execution plans with backpressure.
contribution: Achieves 16 requests/s at 700+ tokens/request with 1ms overhead and 57% P99 latency reduction under multi-pipeline contention.

problem: Dataset bias leads deep learning models to exploit spurious correlations instead of task-relevant signals.
approach: Introduces Standard Anti-Causal Model framework with conditional independence criterion, enabling conditional distance correlation regularization.
contribution: DISCO outperforms or matches bias mitigation approaches with fewer hyperparameters across six datasets and multi-bias scenarios.

problem: Neural operators have opaque latent states and attention-based models can be costly at high resolutions.
approach: Gaussian Particle Operator represents fields with learned Gaussian basis atoms carrying geometric parameters, operating in modal space via PG Gaussian Attention.
contribution: Achieves competitive accuracy against neural operators and Transformers while providing representation-level interpretability.

problem: OCL models are evaluated solely through object discovery and simple reasoning, not regarding compositional generalization and OOD robustness.
approach: Uses instruction-tuned VLMs as scalable evaluators across diverse VQA datasets and introduces unified task jointly assessing localization and usefulness.
contribution: Demonstrates that OCL representation usefulness varies significantly across datasets, establishing more comprehensive evaluation paradigm.

problem: Organizations face rising payments when AI evaluation is noisy, and elaborate evaluation methods' benefits are overshadowed by costs.
approach: Adaptive contracts allow selective detailed evaluation after coarse signals to conserve resources with efficient algorithms for optimal contracts.
contribution: Demonstrates benefits of adaptivity over non-adaptive baselines using question-answering and code-generation datasets.

problem: Visual mechanistic interpretability paradigms exhibit statistical biases and fail to balance interpretability and faithfulness.
approach: Establishes distributional view modeling feature influence on natural image distribution via KL-minimal optimization and energy-guided diffusion.
contribution: Resolves biases under distributional view and demonstrates practical effectiveness on DINOv3 vision models.

problem: Fundamental representational units of LLMs remain undefined, limiting understanding of their mechanisms.
approach: Introduces Atom Theory using atomic inner product metric to define units with criteria for faithfulness and stability identifiable via TSAEs.
contribution: Identifies atoms with near-perfect faithfulness (99.9%) and stability (99.8%) across Gemma2 and Llama3.1 models.

problem: Margin-based preference optimization methods suppress chosen responses while suppressing rejected ones.
approach: Unified incentive-score decomposition reveals local update directions, and disentanglement band identifies when to suppress losers without affecting winners.
contribution: Reward calibration method adaptively rebalances updates to satisfy disentanglement band with better downstream performance.

problem: Model robustness against natural image corruptions requires better understanding of internal computational pathways.
approach: Identifies progressive decay of robust features across layers and proposes S&D refinement using dynamic pathway selection and symmetry-preserving transformations.
contribution: Improves robustness across eight benchmarks with architecture-agnostic, parameter-free approach and zero test-time overhead.

problem: Modern LLMs deployed under compute constraints need flexible capacity control without requiring model-specific architectural modifications.
approach: Plug-and-play framework inducing sparse and low-rank structures during training via augmented Lagrangian and adaptive controller.
contribution: Single training run yields continuous spectrum of model capacities enabling elastic deployment without retraining.
